a.speaker: The hill hospital
a.text:
The generators carried the hospital for eleven hours and then the transfer switch, a box of dead circuit boards, stopped passing their power. Staff are bagging ventilated patients by hand in shifts.

{partner.name} finds you at the ambulance bay, gloves still on. "You came over the hill? Are the kids... okay. Okay." A breath. "I have fourteen patients who can't breathe without someone squeezing a bag."

options.text: "Then I'll squeeze a bag. One shift, and then we go home together."
effects: Night Ward: you took a bagging shift. Two nurses will remember the street that helped.

options.text: "The kids need you. We need you. Please come home."
"Stay. Do the work. Come home when you can."

ward.speaker: Night Ward
ward.text: Squeeze, release, count. Six hours of it, in a corridor lit by headlamps from the shielded supply locker. Some patients die anyway; most don't. At the end of it {partner.name} peels off the gloves and says, "Okay. Home."

ward_fail.speaker: Night Ward
ward_fail.text: You try. Your hands don't know the rhythm and a charge nurse moves you to carrying water instead. It still helps. {partner.name} comes with you at the end of the shift.

comes.speaker: {partner.name}
comes.text: {partner.name} hands the bag to someone else and doesn't look back, which costs more than it looks like it does.

stays.speaker: {partner.name}
stays.text: "Day seven. I'll walk home on day seven, whatever happens." It's a promise. You both know what promises cost now.
